title: Every Terraform Pipeline Has Failed Since Last Night
symptom: No production Terraform run has succeeded this morning: every plan fails within seconds, on every branch, including a pull request that only changes a comment. Nobody is applying anything right now.

goals.description: The state is no longer locked
terraform plan runs and shows no changes

evidence.description: that the run holding the lock is dead

question.prompt: What was the root cause, and why was force-unlock safe?
options: The state file is corrupted and must be restored
An apply cancelled mid-run at 02:14 never released its lock; force-unlock was safe because CI showed that run had ended, so nothing else was writing

debrief: The lock error carries everything you need: the lock's id, who holds it (runner@ci-runner-7), what it was doing (an apply), and since when. CI history showed that apply was cancelled at 02:14, so the process that took the lock no longer exists and never released it. Only then is 'terraform force-unlock <id>' safe; unlocking while a real apply is running lets two writers corrupt the state. '-lock=false' would have worked too, and is worse: it skips the check for everyone after you. Two habits prevent the repeat: let CI cancellation send Terraform an interrupt rather than kill it, and check the plan after unlocking, because an apply cancelled mid-way can leave some resources half-changed.
